431.description: A wood-fired, family-style Asian restaurant known for whole roasted chicken and shareable robata-grilled dishes, from the team behind Bunker Vietnamese.

432.name: Banter
432.description: A casual brunch restaurant in Noho.

433.name: Two Hands
433.description: An Australian-style all-day cafe known for avocado toast, brunch fare, and specialty coffee, part of a small chain with roots in Australia.

434.name: Estela
434.description: A Nolita small-plates restaurant from chef Ignacio Mattos, known for its beef tartare on grilled bread and a well-curated natural wine list in a narrow, always-busy upstairs room.

435.name: The Butcher's Daughter
435.description: A plant-based cafe billed as a 'vegetable slaughterhouse,' serving all-day vegetarian and vegan brunch, juices, and salads in a bright, plant-filled Nolita space.

436.name: Hirohisa
436.description: An intimate Soho restaurant serving multicourse Japanese kaiseki-style tasting menus, recognized with a Michelin star for its refined, seasonal cooking.

438.name: Fiat Café
438.description: A casual Italian cafe in Soho known for brunch fare.

439.name: Atera
439.description: A former two-Michelin-star tasting-menu restaurant in Tribeca known for avant-garde, ingredient-driven cooking served at a communal chef's counter, before it closed in 2022.

440.name: Jungsik
440.description: An elegant Tribeca restaurant from chef Jungsik Yim reinterpreting Korean cuisine through a modern, French-influenced fine-dining lens; has held two Michelin stars.

441.name: L'a Abeille
441.description: A one-Michelin-star Tribeca restaurant blending French technique with Japanese ingredients under chef Mitsunobu Nishida, paired with an adjoining patisserie serving pastries and viennoiserie.

442.name: Sushi of Gari
442.description: A sushi restaurant known for chef's-choice omakase with inventive, sauce-driven preparations that diverge from traditional nigiri, originally opened by chef Masatoshi 'Gari' Sugio.

443.name: Aquavit
443.description: A Scandinavian fine-dining restaurant known for Nordic tasting menus built around dishes like gravlax and herring; chef Emma Bengtsson has been recognized with multiple Michelin stars.

444.name: Benihana
444.description: The original Japanese teppanyaki chain, founded in 1964 by Rocky Aoki, known for hibachi chefs performing tableside knife tricks and the classic onion-volcano flourish.

445.name: Daniel
445.description: Chef Daniel Boulud's flagship Upper East Side restaurant, a longtime pillar of formal French fine dining in New York and a repeat Michelin-starred favorite for special occasions.

446.name: Le Jardinier
446.description: A plant-forward French restaurant from the Jean-Georges Vongerichten group, built around vegetable-driven tasting menus rather than meat or fish as the centerpiece; has held a Michelin star.

447.name: Mediterraneo
447.description: A Mediterranean restaurant on the Upper East Side.

448.name: Quality Italian
448.description: Part of the Quality Branded restaurant group, known for playful, oversized riffs on Italian-American classics like chicken parm served upright on a stand.

449.name: Quality Meats
449.description: A modern steakhouse from the Quality Branded group, known for contemporary decor and creative touches like brown-butter bread service alongside classic steaks.

450.name: Scalinatella
450.description: A longstanding white-tablecloth Italian restaurant tucked into an Upper East Side townhouse basement, known for classic Northern Italian dishes and a loyal uptown following.

451.name: Sushi Noz
451.description: An intimate, high-end omakase counter from chef Nozomu Abe, among the pricier and more exclusive sushi experiences on the Upper East Side.

452.name: Toloache
452.description: An upscale Mexican restaurant from chef Julian Medina's restaurant group, known for tableside guacamole, tacos, and an extensive tequila and mezcal list.

453.name: Hutong
453.description: An upscale Northern Chinese restaurant known for Peking duck and dramatic, lantern-lit decor, part of a restaurant group with sister locations in Hong Kong and London.

454.name: The East Pole
454.description: A New American restaurant on the Upper East Side from the team behind The Fat Radish, known for seasonal, vegetable-forward cooking and a popular weekend brunch.

455.name: Fiorello's
455.description: A classic Italian trattoria across from Lincoln Center, popular with the pre-theater and concert crowd for thin-crust pizza, a raw bar, and old-school hospitality.

456.name: Le Trois Chevaux
456.description: A romantic French restaurant in the West Village from chef Angie Mar, formerly of The Beatrice Inn, known for opulent, meat-forward dishes and dramatic presentations.

457.name: Moustache
457.description: A longtime West Village favorite for Palestinian and Middle Eastern comfort food, especially its 'pitza' -- pita topped like a pizza -- alongside hummus and lamb dishes.

458.name: Cafe Panino
458.description: A casual West Village spot serving panini sandwiches.

459.name: Jungsik
459.description: An elegant Tribeca restaurant from chef Jungsik Yim reinterpreting Korean cuisine through a modern, French-influenced fine-dining lens; has held two Michelin stars.

460.name: Chambers
460.description: New American restaurant in Tribeca known for chef Jonathan Karis's seasonal small plates and Pascaline Lepeltier's sprawling wine program of over 2,000 bottles; named to the NYT's 100 Best Restaurants list.

461.name: Ho Foods
461.description: Ten-seat East Village counter known for Taiwanese beef noodle soup made with pasture-raised beef, house-fermented mustard greens, and a 24-hour bone broth; frequently cited among the city's best bowls.

462.name: Kisa
462.description: Lower East Side Korean diner modeled on 1980s 'kisa sikdang' driver's restaurants: pick one entree, like bulgogi or bibimbap, and get rice, soup, and bottomless rotating banchan.

463.name: Borgo
463.description: Wood-fired, Tuscan-leaning trattoria from restaurateur Andrew Tarlow's team, his first Manhattan spot, known for a timballo di anelletti pasta bake and hearth-fired focaccia in a candlelit dining room.

464.name: Bridges
464.description: Michelin-starred New American restaurant in Chinatown, in the space that housed dim sum institution Hop Shing for decades, from chef Sam Lawrence (ex-Estela), known for a Comté-chanterelle tart and sea urchin custard.

465.name: Bungalow
465.description: Elaborate Indian restaurant from Michelin-starred chef Vikas Khanna, set in a jewel-toned, members'-club-style room, spanning regional dishes and family recipes; earned three stars from the New York Times.

466.name: Attoboy
466.description: Industrial-leaning Flatiron Korean spot from chef Junghyun 'JP' Park and Ellia Park, serving an approachable four-course prix fixe with dishes like kimchi-brined fried chicken and inventive seafood plates.

467.name: Kabawa
467.description: Caribbean fine-dining restaurant from chef Paul Carmichael in the former Momofuku Ko space, serving a prix fixe of dishes like roti, cassava dumplings, and jerk duck sausage; named a top U.S. restaurant by Food & Wine.

468.name: Ha's Snack Bar
468.description: Tiny, hard-to-book Lower East Side wine bar where chefs Anthony Ha and Sadie Mae Burns-Ha filter French bistro classics through a Vietnamese lens, with dishes like pate chaud and tamarind-butter snails.

469.name: Sushi Sho
469.description: Three-Michelin-starred Edomae sushi counter near Bryant Park from chef Keiji Nakazawa, relocated from Waikiki; the first NYC sushi restaurant to reach three stars since Masa, with just ten seats.

470.name: Cho Dang Gol
470.description: Longtime Midtown Korean spot serving handmade tofu since 1997 in the style of a Korean coastal village, especially prized for its soondubu jjigae; a Michelin Bib Gourmand pick.

471.name: Cocina Consuelo
471.description: Tiny, walk-in-only Hamilton Heights spot from chef Karina García and husband Lalo Rodríguez, serving Mexican dishes rooted in his grandmother's recipes, including birria-topped bone marrow and masa pancakes.

472.name: Dhamaka
472.description: Lower East Side restaurant from Unapologetic Foods (Chintan Pandya and Roni Mazumdar) serving bold regional Indian dishes rarely found stateside, including a noted braised rabbit; landed on the NYT's 100 Best list.

473.name: Four Twenty Five
473.description: Jean-Georges Vongerichten and Jonathan Benno's soaring Park Avenue dining room, pairing French, Italian, and Asian influences in dishes like kampachi with aji amarillo and handmade rabbit agnolotti.

474.name: Frenchette
474.description: Classic Tribeca brasserie from chefs Riad Nasr and Lee Hanson, known for duck frites, roast chicken, and a deep natural wine list; won the James Beard Award for Best New Restaurant.

475.name: Great N.Y. Noodletown
475.description: No-frills, cash-only Chinatown institution open since 1981, serving classic Cantonese roast meats with ginger-scallion sauce and shrimp wonton soup; a longtime late-night favorite among chefs.

476.name: Houseman
476.description: Neighborhood New American spot in Hudson Square from chef-owner Ned Baldwin (ex-Prune), known for a thick burger and roast chicken in a cozy room with reclaimed bowling-alley maple tables.

477.name: King
477.description: South Village bistro from chefs Clare de Boer and Jess Shadbolt (both ex-River Café London), serving a daily-changing, greenmarket-driven menu of Southern French and Italian dishes like panisse and house-made ravioli.

478.name: Le Veau d'Or
478.description: New York's oldest French bistro, open since 1937 and revived in 2024 by Frenchette's Riad Nasr and Lee Hanson; fifteen tables serving Escoffier-inspired classics like tête de veau.

479.name: Little Myanmar
479.description: Family-run East Village Burmese spot known for tea leaf salad, yellow noodle salad, and Burmese pancakes; largely halal with numerous vegan options on a surprisingly large menu.

480.name: Lola's
480.description: Chef Suzanne Cupps's (Gramercy Tavern, Untitled) first solo restaurant near the Flatiron Building, blending Southern and pan-Asian influences and named for her Filipino grandmother, in a jade-tiled dining room.

481.name: Mắm
481.description: Lower East Side Vietnamese spot specializing in Central Vietnamese food, known for bún đậu mắm tôm and a phở praised as among the city's best; low-stool, communal seating.

482.name: Okdongsik
482.description: NYC outpost of chef Ok Dongsik's Michelin Bib Gourmand Seoul restaurant, built around one dish, dwaeji gukbap (pork rib and rice soup), plus kimchi mandu; hides the speakeasy bar George Bang Bang inside.

484.name: Raku
484.description: A Japanese restaurant in the East Village.

485.name: Shukette
485.description: A Middle Eastern restaurant in Chelsea.

488.name: Una Pizza Napoletana
488.description: A pizza restaurant on the Lower East Side.

489.name: Yoon Haeundae Galbi
489.description: A Korean restaurant in Midtown West.

490.name: White Bear
490.description: A Chinese restaurant in Flushing, Queens.

491.name: Xie Bao
491.description: A Chinese restaurant in Flushing, Queens.

492.name: Szechuan Mountain House
492.description: A Sichuan Chinese restaurant in Flushing, Queens.

493.name: Alley 41
493.description: A Chinese restaurant in Flushing, Queens.

494.name: Old Sport
494.description: A halal Chinese restaurant in Forest Hills, Queens.

495.name: Levant
495.description: A Middle Eastern restaurant in Astoria, Queens.

496.name: Temple Canteem
